Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)
Referred Sections: CMM-601.4: Initial Primary Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF)

Required findings: Significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.) AND unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability

ANY of the following: dermatomal sensory deficit, motor deficit (e.g., biceps, triceps weakness), reflex changes, shoulder abduction relief sign, nerve root tension sign (e.g., Spurling's maneuver), or unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity without concordant objective physical exam findings

MRI/CT shows neural structure compression at the requested level(s) that is concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings and that is caused by ANY of the following: herniated disc(s) (retained disc material or a recurrent disc herniation), synovial cyst or arachnoid cyst, central/lateral/foraminal stenosis, or osteophytes

Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for six (6) weeks; provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician) for six (6) weeks; or epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) performed at the same level(s) as the requested surgery

Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders) AND documentation of nicotine-free status (never-smoker or refrained from smoking/nicotine for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods)

Required findings: ANY of the following: upper/lower extremity weakness, numbness, or pain; fine motor dysfunction (buttoning, handwriting, clumsiness of hands); gait disturbance; new-onset bowel or bladder dysfunction; or frequent falls

ANY of the following: grip and release test, ataxic gait, hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, Babinski sign, tandem walking test demonstrating ataxia, inverted brachial radial reflex, increased muscle tone or spasticity, clonus, or myelopathic hand

MRI/CT shows findings that are concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings and that are caused by EITHER of the following: cervical spinal cord compression or cervical spinal stenosis

Non-Indications: Radiculopathy: Failure to demonstrate less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least two of the required conservative management options (medications, exercise, or injections) for the required duration, unless contraindicated
Radiculopathy: Presence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)
Radiculopathy: Failure to document nicotine-free status (never-smoker or 6+ weeks abstinence validated by objective cotinine testing)
Radiculopathy: MRI/CT findings that are not concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings
Myelopathy: MRI/CT findings that are not concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings
Important criteria & exceptions: For Radiculopathy, conservative management exceptions apply if the required treatments are contraindicated
For Radiculopathy, nicotine-free status must be validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab
For Radiculopathy, epidural steroid injections or selective nerve root blocks must be performed at the same level(s) as the requested surgery to count toward the conservative management trial
Documentation required: Plain x-rays of the cervical spine including flexion/extension lateral views (for Radiculopathy)
MRI or CT report showing neural structure compression or spinal cord compression/stenosis concordant with symptoms and physical exam findings

Records of conservative management including prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, NSAIDs, provider-directed exercise program, or epidural steroid injections/selective nerve root blocks (for Radiculopathy)
Objective cotinine testing results (serum, urinary, or saliva) verifying normal range for nicotine-free status (for Radiculopathy)
Documentation of absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (for Radiculopathy)
